quotes.text: Use this guide to learn the different ways to build your subscriptions integration, and follow the links to in-depth, step-by-step guides.
Use [Metronome](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/usage-based.md) to configure more complex pricing models based on usage.
Supports the following payment methods: Link, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Klarna, and Amazon Pay.
1Payment links aren’t supported for usage-based billing.
| **Freemium** | Allow customers access to your product or service without requesting payment information.

old_evidence.text: **Credit burndown pricing**: You collect prepayment for your usage-based product or service, and allow customers to apply [billing credits](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based/billing-credits.md) as they use your product or service.
- Supports the following payment methods: Link, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, Klarna, and Amazon Pay.
1Payment links aren’t supported for usage-based billing.

findings: Both same-URL captures describe a decision guide, not an implementation or payment outcome: choose pricing, checkout interface and payment timing, then follow a use-case link (old 4-12, 156-167; new 5-13, 172-183). The current [[source-stripe-subscriptions-design-integration]] accurately summarizes the four/seven/three structure and already routes through wiki/index.md:7 → wiki/stripe-index.md:608 and reciprocally from wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md:215.

The four pricing categories and subtypes are unchanged (old 18-51; new 19-65), but the November usage-based row explicitly points to Metronome for more complex pricing (new 48-65). This is dated guide wording, not a requirement to use Metronome for every usage-based subscription and not evidence that an integration gained a new payment capability.

The seven checkout interface categories and six named one-click methods remain the same (old 53-120; new 67-136). Payment links remain excluded from usage-based billing in this guide (old 120; new 136, 183). The November no-code Dashboard sentence and revised image/table formatting clarify or present existing navigation rather than establish a newly launched interface.

Pay-up-front, free-trial and freemium rows remain typical flow illustrations (old 122-154; new 138-170). The same six use-case matrix rows still route flat-rate trials, usage-based checkout, pricing tables, flat-rate payment links, mobile flat-rate checkout and one-click buttons (old 156-165; new 172-181). New ui=full-page query parameters on two trial links select a documentation variant, not a changed subscription contract.
substantive_changes: The November guide explicitly recommends Metronome for more complex usage pricing in its usage-based table cell (new 48-65), whereas the May table describes usage-based models and billing credits without naming Metronome there (old 40-51). Add this as a dated, conditional product-navigation detail in the source summary.

November replaces screenshot-oriented pricing examples with textual flat-rate, per-seat, tiered and usage/credit arithmetic (new 19-65; old 23-51). These are illustrative values and revised presentation, not new pricing-model requirements.

November states payment links can be created and shared without code from the Dashboard (new 114-126); May already described reusable hosted links and the usage-based exclusion (old 100-120). The addition clarifies workflow, not a new interface or universal no-code setup guarantee.
November's matrix adds ui=full-page to two free-trial documentation links (new 176; old 160). Other use-case rows retain their meaning (new 177-181; old 161-165).
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 12, 2026 already listed four pricing models, all seven interface types, six one-click method names, the payment-link usage-based exclusion, three timing models and six example integration routes (old 18-21, 53-120, 122-167). Do not reclassify these as November launches.

May's credit-burndown wording linked billing credits and gave a different price/tier example (old 40-51); preserve its dated evidence separately from November's illustrative token arithmetic and Metronome reference (new 48-65).
The existing source's note that nine image assets were not downloaded is a May ingest/provenance note (source 15, 53), not a November product limitation or an inference from the new capture.
conflicts: Current source line 32 says the custom Elements payment form offers 'full layout control'; both raws only say that the Payment Element layout can be customized to fit the checkout flow and appearance adjusted via the Appearance API (old 75-82; new 89-96). Narrow the claim if refreshing this source.

Current source line 36 names Payment Sheet and says 'or custom' for mobile. The capture describes a prebuilt sheet or customizable drop-in component (old 111-118; new 127-134) and matrix links to iOS, Android and React Native instructions (old 164; new 180); do not infer every native SDK's current supported UI or subscription eligibility from this design index.

The concept's top-level design decision list at wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md:12 matches the old/new category map. Any update about Metronome should be a dated source-level navigation note, not an unqualified replacement of that broad concept or proof that all listed one-click methods are available to a particular merchant.
unresolved_questions: The static design-guide captures do not establish selected UI/platform query variant behavior, account eligibility, payment method availability, actual invoice/payment status, or live feature rollout.
The new Metronome wording does not specify which complex usage models require it or whether simpler Stripe Billing usage models are unsupported.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/design-an-integration, [[source-stripe-subscriptions-design-integration]] should identify a design guide that asks merchants to choose among four pricing models, seven checkout interfaces and three payment-timing models, then follow six example use-case routes (new 9-13, 19-65, 67-181). The May capture already contained those categories, the six named one-click methods and payment-link exclusion for usage-based billing (old 18-21, 53-120, 156-167), which the current source largely summarizes at lines 13-44. The November usage row newly names Metronome for more complex pricing (new 48), but the guide's typical flows and example matrix do not prove account eligibility, execution, payment or provisioning success.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/design-an-integration, [[source-stripe-subscriptions-design-integration]] warrants a bounded dated update for the November Metronome guidance on complex usage-based pricing (new 48-65 versus old 40-51). Added arithmetic examples, no-code payment-link sentence, cleaner tables and ui=full-page trial-link parameters are primarily explanatory or navigation changes (new 19-65, 114-126, 176; old 23-51, 100-120, 160). Preserve May's existing seven-interface and timing-model evidence (old 53-154) and its image provenance. Qualify the current source's 'full layout control' and mobile UI wording (source 32, 36) against both captures (new 89-96, 127-134; old 75-82, 111-118). Payment-link exclusion remains in both (new 136, 183; old 120, 167); none of these captures proves method availability, merchant eligibility, invoice creation or paid funds.
